questions.question: Amarnath invested a sum of Rs. 22,500. At what rate of simple interest per annum will he obtain a total amount of Rs. 28,800 at the end of 4 years?
questions.solution:
Given:

Amarnath invested a sum of Rs. 22,500.

Time = 4 years

Amount becomes = Rs. 28800

Concept used:

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P + SI

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

Calculation:

Let the rate of interest be R%.

According to the question,

22500 + (22500 × R × 4)/100 = 28800

⇒ (22500 × R)/25 = 28800 - 22500

⇒ (900 × R) = 6300

⇒ R = 6300/900

⇒ R = 7

**∴ At 7% rate of simple interest per annum he will obtain a total amount of Rs. 28,800 at the end of 4 years.**

questions.question: A certain sum amounts to Rs. 13860 after 5 years and to Rs. 16776 after 8 years at the same rate per cent per annum at simple interest. What will be simple interest (in Rs.) on a sum of Rs. 20,000 for 3 (2)/(5) years at the same rate?
questions.solution:
Given:

A certain sum amounts to Rs. 13860 after 5 years and to Rs. 16776 after 8 years at the same rate per cent per annum at simple interest. 

Concept used:

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P + SI

where, P = Principal amount, R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

3 (2)/(5) years = 3.4 years

Calculation:

Let the rate of interest be R%.

Interest incurred in 3 years = 16776 - 13860 = Rs. 2916

Internet incurred per year = 2916/3 = Rs. 972

So, the principal amount = 13860 - 972 × 5 = Rs. 9000

According to the concept,

(9000 × R × 1)/100 = 972

⇒ R = 97200/9000

⇒ R = 10.8

Now, the simple interest incurred on Rs. 20,000 for 3 (2)/(5) years at the same rate

⇒ (20000 × 10.8 × 3.4)/100

⇒ Rs. 7344

**∴ The simple interest incurred on Rs. 20,000 for 3 (2)/(5) years at the same rate is Rs. 7344.**

questions.question: A certain sum of money becomes 4 times in 12 years when invested at simple interest. In how many years will it become 10 times of itself at the same rate?
questions.solution:
Given:

The principal amount becomes 4 times in 12 years when invested at simple interest.

Concept used:

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

Calculation:

Let the principal amount be Rs. P and the rate of interest be R%.

According to the question,

(P × R × 12)/100 = 4P - P

⇒ R = 25%

Let the time taken for the principal amount to be 10 times of itself be T.

According to the question,

(P × 25 × T)/100 = 10P - P

⇒ T = 36

**∴ In 36 years the principal amount will become 10 times itself at the same rate. **

Total amount = Rs.16,000

Total interest earn = Rs.6024

simple interest = (p × r × t)/100

where p, r and t are principal, rate and time respectively

**Calculation**

let the amount given to Rahul is Rs. x

and the amount given to Vinod is Rs(16000 - x)

simple interest = (x × 7.5 × 4)/100

⇒ 30x/100

Vinod simple interest = [(16000 - x) × 12 × 4]/100

According to question

questions.question: A certain sum amounts to ₹12,740 in 4 years and to ₹15,925 in {7{1 over 2}} years at the same rate percentage per annum at simple interest. The sum (in ₹) and the rate percentage per annum, respectively are:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The first amount = Rs.12740 in 4 years

The second amount = Rs.15925 in {7{1 over 2}} years

The rate is the same for both amounts and is calculated at simple interest.

**Formula used:**

Simple interest = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P × (1 + RT/100)

Where P = principal, R = Rate of interest, T = time 

**Calculation:**

Let the Rate of interest be R % and the Principal be P

Then, according to the formula 

⇒ 12740 = P × (1 + (4R)/100) ---(1)

also, 15925 = P × (1 + 15R/200) ---(2)

On dividing both the equations, we get

12740/15925 = 2 × (100 + 4R)/(200 + 15R)

⇒ 4/5 = 2 × (100 + 4R)/(200 + 15R)

⇒ (100 + 4R)/(200 + 15R) = 2/5

⇒ 5 × (100 + 4R) = 2 × (200 + 15R)

⇒ 500 + 20R = 400 + 30R

⇒ 10R = 100 

⇒ R = 10%

Now, from equation (1)

12740 = P × (1 + 40/100)

⇒ P = 12740 × 100/140

⇒ P = Rs.9100

**∴ Principal = Rs.9100 and Rate percentage per annum = 10%.**

questions.question: A certain sum amounts to Rs. 13200 after 4 years and to Rs. 16400 after 8 years at the same rate per cent p.a. at simple interest. The simple interest (in Rs.) on the same sum at 10% p.a. for 3(1)/(5) years will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A certain sum amounts to Rs. 13200 after 4 years and to Rs. 16400 after 8 years

**Concept used:**

S.I = (P × T × R)/100

P = Principal or sum

T = time

R = rate

**Calculation:**

As we know in simple interest the interest is always constant if the rate and sum are same

So, Interest for 4 years = 16400 - 13200

⇒ Rs. 3200

So, for the 1st 4 years, the interest will be Rs. 3200 [As mentioned earlier interest will be the same]

So, sum = 13200 - 3200

⇒ Rs. 10000

Now,

S.I = (10000 × 10 × 16)/(100 × 5)

⇒ 100 × 2 × 16

⇒ Rs. 3200

**∴ The simple interest (in Rs.) on the same sum at 10% p.a. for 3(1)/(5) years will be 3200.**
